task: Add default-project assignment and display to the User Management UI (widen a permission gate, extend the frontend type, add two store methods against already-live endpoints, and update three components).

key_reasoning.reason: Base risk is low (S) — every touch point copies an exact existing pattern (Valtio CRUD shape, DetailsBadge icon prop, controlled popup, (isAdmin || isMaintainer) idiom used 8+ times already). Bumped to M by the authorization red flag: UserDetailsPopup.tsx's canManageProjects gate is widened from super-admin-only to admin-or-maintainer, changing who can manage project assignments.

Five concrete ACs and an explicit out-of-scope list, but two open decisions remain before implementation: AC5's 'plain user' wording doesn't match a reachable role under today's tab-visibility gate (auditor is the concrete case, needs confirming), and the optimistic-update UX for a default moving from one row to another (two-row visual change vs. refetch) isn't specified.

Six files touched across three conceptual layers (presentation: UsersManagementPage.tsx, UserProjectsTable.tsx, AddProjectPopup.tsx, UserDetailsPopup.tsx; type: user.ts; store: store/user.ts) — more than a single self-contained component, but all within one admin feature area with no new abstractions.

UI (four components) + Store/service (two new Valtio methods) + the already-live backend endpoints they call — a standard full-stack path (UI + Service + API) even though the backend side itself needs no changes.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S to M: the permission-gate widen affects authorization (who can manage a user's project assignments), per the 'affects authentication or authorization' red flag.
